newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CBO sees 1997 growth of 2.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CBO sees 1997 growth of 2.3 percent.

text.p: The Congressional Budget Office Thursday issued preliminary economic projections that showed an expectation of higher economic growth in 1997 and lower inflation than previously forecast.

CBO forecast 2.3 percent gross domestic product growth for 1997, compared 1.9 percent growth that the agency had forecast in its May report. CBO's consumer price index forecast for 1997 edged lower to 2.9 percent from 3.1 percent in the May report.
The 1997 unemployment rate was forecast to average 5.3 percent, a much lower projection than the 6.0 percent expected in the May CBO report.
The three-month Treasury bill rate was forecast to average 5.0 percent next year, compared with 4.8 percent in the previous CBO forecast.
The 10-year Treasury note rate was forecast to average 6.2 percent in 1997, compared with the 6.4 percent previous CBO projection.

The projections will be used to construct CBO's budget projections that are to be published at the end of January, and could be revised if "compelling" new economic information is received before those budget projections are completed, CBO said.

Also, the projections "assume that current budgetary policy will continue, and therefore they do not reflect the effects on economic growth and interest rates of a policy intended to balance the budget," CBO said.
